title: Poset-refined majorization relations
authors: Alexander E. Guterman, Michael M. Wolf
abstract: Several classical majorization relations for sums or products of matrices involve a majorizing vector of perfectly aligned eigenvalues or singular values. By relaxing the order of alignment to a partial order, we show that the majorization can be strengthened, provided the change-of-basis matrices admit an LU-approximation with respect to this partial order. In this way, we obtain refined versions of Ky Fan's majorization relations, Horn's log-majorization relation, and von Neumann's trace inequality. As an application, we give a short proof of the separable Ky Fan majorization relation for an arbitrary number of tensor factors and extend it to a sum of tensor products of arbitrary matrices. Further applications concern majorization relations for sums of (anti-)symmetric powers and for products of Kronecker sums.
summary: This theoretical paper refines classical majorization relations by incorporating partial order structures from posets into matrix analysis. It proves new, tighter bounds for the eigenvalues and singular values of sums and products of matrices. The work is significant for developing more precise mathematical tools applicable to spectral problems in quantum physics.
main_problem: The paper aims to refine classical majorization relations, such as those for eigenvalues or singular values of sums and products of matrices, by replacing the strict linear order with a partial order (poset). This refinement strengthens existing mathematical bounds.
main_result: New refined majorization inequalities are established for spectral properties ($\lambda$ or $\sigma$) when the underlying structure is governed by a poset admitting an LU-approximation. These refinements improve upon classical results like Ky Fan's and Horn's relations.
method: The methodology involves leveraging concepts from partially ordered sets (posets) to define matrix structures ($L(P), U(P)$) and proving inequalities using determinant properties, Cauchy-Binet formulas, and analyzing the structure of compound matrices.
model_or_system: The analysis is highly abstract, focusing on general mathematical structures involving Hermitian or positive semidefinite matrices whose entries are indexed by a poset $P$. Applications include sums and products related to tensor factors and Kronecker sums.
key_observables: Eigenvalues ($\lambda$) and singular values ($\sigma$), spectral functions $\alpha$ and $ eta$, and matrix norms/traces ($	ext{tr}[\cdot]$).
important_parameters: The structure of the poset $P$ (especially whether it is linearly ordered) and the existence of an LU-approximation for change-of-basis matrices.
main_assumptions: The majorization refinement holds only if the relevant change-of-basis matrix admits an LU-approximation with respect to the considered partial order.
figures_summary: No figures were described in the notes, but the text references theorems and corollaries establishing specific inequalities (e.g., $\sigma(A+B) \prec_w \lambda(D_{\alpha+ eta})$).
paper_structure: The paper builds from general poset theory to establish a core theorem relating LU-approximability to refined majorization for sums of matrices. It then applies this framework sequentially to specific physical/mathematical contexts: Ky Fan relations (sums), Horn log-majorization (products), and finally, symmetric tensors and Kronecker sums.
why_interesting: While highly mathematical, the generalization of spectral inequalities using poset structures provides powerful tools for bounding quantities in quantum systems where interactions or couplings are naturally partially ordered (e.g., certain tensor product decompositions).
